newsitem.title: USA: US companies eager to switch phone service - study.
newsitem.headline: US companies eager to switch phone service - study.

text.p: Many large corporations plan to drop their existing local telephone company and switch to a long-distance carrier for local service, according to a survey issued Wednesday.

The survey of 500 "decision makers" by Deloitte & Touche Consulting Group also showed that 75 percent of large business customers indicate they would prefer to use long-distance carriers over all other carriers to meet their "one-stop" shopping needs in the new Communications Age.
Only 21 percent favored local phone companies.

Thirty percent said they plan to switch to a new local carrier from their existing local company, assuming equal levels of service and price. Of those that intend to switch, 77 percent expect to go to a long-distance carrier.
Deloitte & Touche officials said the survey results spell bad news for the regional Baby Bell phone companies and other local carriers.
"If they lose this kind of market share, it would have a devastating impact on their profitability," said Steven Martin, a principal at Deloitte & Touche.

Dwight Allen, a Deloitte & Touche associate national director, said the results suggest long-distance carriers -- such as AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Corp and Sprint Corp -- have "an edge" heading into the new competition era following enactment earlier this year of the big telecommunications law.
The law breaks down decades-old barriers and allows the different industries to get into each other's businesses.
When comparing long-distance and local carriers, those surveyed expressed more satisfaction with the long-distance companies by a 2 to 1 margin.
But the officials added that the study shows that both groups need to improve their performance.
"Unprecedented levels of provider performance and innovation will be required to win and retain those sophisticated and demanding customers," said Robert Mayer, senior manager at Deloitte & Touche.
